title: A bag left on a coach
prompt:
You recently travelled on a long-distance coach and left a bag on board when you got off.

Write a letter to the coach company. In your letter

- give details of your journey
- describe the bag and what was in it
- explain what you would like the company to do

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:

Dear Sir or Madam,
tips: The reader is a stranger at a company, so keep the tone formal: no contractions, no slang, and close with 'Yours faithfully'.
Give the details staff would actually need to find the bag: date, route, departure time, seat number or where you were sitting.
Describe the bag precisely (colour, size, brand, distinguishing features) and say why the contents matter to you.
The third bullet asks for action. Make a clear, polite request and give practical options, such as collection or posting.
Use one paragraph per bullet point plus a short opening and closing. That covers all three points and organises the letter.

samples.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to inform you that I left my bag on one of your coach last week and I hope you can help me to find it.

I travelled from Manchester to London on Friday 14 March. The coach leave Manchester at 8.30 in the morning and arrived to Victoria Coach Station at around 1 pm. I was sitting near the back, I think it was seat 32. When I got off I was in hurry because my friend was waiting me, so I forgot my bag on the shelf above the seat.

The bag is a small black backpack with a red zip. Inside there is my laptop, a charger and a blue notebook with my university notes. The notebook is very important for me because I have exams next month and I can not study without it.

Could you please check if someone found the bag? If you find it, I would like you to send it to my address. I can pay for the postage if it is necessary. Also please contact me as soon as possible.

I am looking forward to hear from you.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Kowalski
samples.commentary: Task Achievement: all three bullets are covered and the purpose is clear, with useful details such as the date, route and seat. The request is relevant but basic, and the writer never gives a phone number or email even though he asks to be contacted. The tone is mostly formal and appropriate. Coherence and Cohesion: one paragraph per bullet gives clear organisation, but linking is simple and repetitive ('so', 'also', 'if'). Lexical Resource: vocabulary is adequate for the task ('postage', 'charger') but plain, with little precision. Grammatical Range and Accuracy: a mix of simple and complex sentences, with frequent errors that do not block meaning: 'one of your coach', 'The coach leave', 'arrived to', 'in hurry', 'waiting me', 'looking forward to hear'. These are typical of Band 6.

samples.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing because I accidentally left a bag on one of your coaches last Friday, and I would be very grateful for your help in recovering it.

I was travelling on the 8.30 am service from Manchester to London Victoria on 14 March, which arrived at about 1 pm. I was sitting in seat 32, towards the back of the coach. As my friend was waiting for me outside the station, I got off in a hurry and only realised an hour later that I had left my bag on the luggage rack above my seat.

It is a small black backpack with a red zip and a university logo on the front pocket. It contains my laptop, its charger and a blue notebook. Although the laptop is valuable, the notebook is what really worries me, as it holds all my revision notes for exams next month.

I would therefore like to ask whether the bag has been handed in to your lost property office. If it has, I could collect it from Victoria, or alternatively I would be happy to pay for it to be posted to me. You can reach me on 07700 914 286 or at d.kowalski@mailbox.com.

Thank you in advance for your assistance.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Kowalski
samples.commentary: Task Achievement: all bullets are fully addressed and extended. The writer explains why the notebook matters, offers two practical options and gives contact details, so the purpose is clear and the tone is consistently formal. Coherence and Cohesion: logical paragraphing and a good range of linkers ('As', 'Although', 'therefore', 'alternatively') used naturally. Lexical Resource: precise and appropriate vocabulary ('luggage rack', 'lost property office', 'handed in', 'revision notes'), with some less common items. Grammatical Range and Accuracy: a variety of complex structures (relative clauses, 'only realised... that I had left', passive 'has been handed in') with good control and only minor slips. It falls short of Band 8 mainly because the phrasing is accurate but not especially flexible, and some sentences follow a predictable pattern.

samples.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to ask for your help in tracing a bag that I left on one of your coaches on Friday 14 March.

I was a passenger on the 8.30 am service from Manchester to London Victoria, which reached Victoria shortly before 1 pm. I had seat 32, three rows from the back on the left-hand side. Because a friend was waiting for me, I left the coach in something of a rush, and it was not until I reached her flat that I realised my bag was still on the overhead rack.

The bag is a compact black backpack with a red zip, and the front pocket carries the crest of Manchester University. Inside are a silver laptop, its charger and a blue A4 notebook. While the laptop is obviously worth the most, it is the notebook that I am most anxious to recover: it contains several months of handwritten revision notes for exams that begin in four weeks, and these would be impossible to replace.

I would be grateful if you could check whether the bag was found when the coach was cleaned, and let me know which lost property office it has been sent to. I am able to collect it in person from Victoria at short notice; failing that, I would gladly cover the cost of sending it by recorded delivery. I can be contacted on 07700 914 286 or at d.kowalski@mailbox.com.

Thank you for your time, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Kowalski
samples.commentary: Task Achievement: every bullet is covered thoroughly with relevant, well-chosen detail (exact seat position, distinguishing crest, why the notes cannot be replaced), and the request is specific and realistic. The formal tone is maintained throughout. Coherence and Cohesion: information is sequenced very logically and cohesion is managed smoothly ('it was not until... that', 'While', 'failing that') without overuse of linkers. Lexical Resource: a wide, natural range ('tracing', 'in something of a rush', 'distinguishing', 'recorded delivery', 'at short notice') used precisely. Grammatical Range and Accuracy: a wide range of structures, including a cleft sentence ('it is the notebook that I am most anxious to recover') and a 'not until' structure, almost entirely error-free. It is not Band 9 because a few phrases are slightly formulaic and the letter does not quite show full, effortless flexibility.
